svg.title: AnyScan architecture
svg.desc: AnyScan finds every object on a work surface, describes it and measures it. A catalogue mode also judges it. In every mode the camera shows a live preview while parts are placed, then takes a fresh frame once nothing moves, undistorted. Two cues, fused, find the objects: what differs from the empty surface, and a segmentation model. Each object is described in words by a local vision-language model and measured in mm through the calibration, and the desktop application shows the result in its Live, Trends, History and Log views. A catalogue mode adds four steps for each object found. It recognises the catalogued part by its reference images. Only a part wholly inside the inspection area is judged, and one outside is told apart as a part or a foreign object by similarity, size and colour. A judged part is checked on the side that is up, told by its references or else by its countersinks: its size, its holes, each bore centred in its countersink with the view angle corrected, and its stains. Each object then gets a state: OK, NOK or Warning, a Warning with its kind: outside the area, a foreign object, several parts, or a side unclear or mismatched. In a catalogue mode each object is described after its state, told what the checks found, and a sentence that contradicts them is dropped. The stages are set up by the mode (models and prompts), which names its station (camera, light, table and inspection area). The station names its calibration (undistortion and mm per pixel) and the empty-surface reference, and a catalogue mode also names its catalogue item (the part, its checks and its reference images). Every analysis is recorded with its images and results, alongside the session log, a run summary and the daily station events. Developed within internal research at JIC Smart Factory. Funded by the European Union.
